Shady Guy: Sells rare services for Battle Points. This includes being able to change any Pokémon into its shiny form · Upper exterior area at Battle Frontier between 11:59 PM and 4:49 AM
Egg Move Tutor: Teaches a selected Pokémon its evolution family's egg moves · 15 Battle Points · Standing behind the stall west of the Battle Frontier entrance

Hidden Power Changer: Changes a Pokémon's Hidden Power type & allows you to see all Hidden Power types of the Pokémon in your party · 15 Battle Points · Standing behind a stall south of the main Battle Frontier building
EV Checker & Changer: Maximizes or purges one of the select Pokémon's EVs · 50 BP · Behind a stall in the top-right corner of the area
Move Relearner: Allows a selected Pokémon to relearn any forgotten move · 1 Move = 1 Heart Scale · Inside the house in the southeast corner of town
Evolution Stone Creator: Creates any type of rare Evolution Stone in exchange for Everstones · 4 Everstones · Directly east of the main Cube Corp. building
Master Ball Maker: Gives you a Master Ball in exchange for Gems · 30 Gems (same type) · Standing behind the southwest stall in the Cube Corp. exterior area
Poke Ball Changer: Changes the Poke Ball the select Pokémon is held in · 1 Ring Target · Standing behind the stall directly west of the main Cube Corp. building
Beast Ball Maker: Creates Beast Balls in exchange for Iron Balls · 1 Iron Ball · Standing behind the northeast stall in the Cube Corp. area
Sinnoh Starters Lady: Gives players the Sinnoh starters for free · Inside of the house that's directly southeast of the Rift Cave entrance
Happiness Increaser: Plays with the selected Pokemon in the player's party to increase its overall happiness · free · Inside of the house directly south of the Rift Cave entrance
Rare Bone Maniac: Purchases rare bones from you for 10,000 Poke Dollars · 10,000 Poke Dollars (paid to you) · Inside of the house east of the Dehara City Gym
Ore Maniac: Purchases all types of ores from you · Inside of the house directly east of the Dehara City Gym
Happiness Checker: Checks the happiness of the first Pokémon in the player's party · free · Inside of the house directly south of the Rift Cave entrance
Move Deleter: Allows you to delete any Pokémon's moves, including HMs · free · Inside of the house northwest of the Epidimy Town Pokémon Center
Togepi Egg Lady: Gives you a Togepi egg for free · Inside the house directly east of the Fallshore City Poke Mart
Lucky Egg Upgrader: Upgrades the player's Lucky Eggs in exchange for Big Pearls and Pearl Strings · Depends on the Lucky Egg's level · Inside of the Fallshore City Mission HQ
Food Maniac: Purchases food items and berries from the player · Standing on the very south side of the Dehara City Mall's second floor
Relic Maniac: Purchases all relics from the player · Inside of the house directly behind the Gurun Town Pokémon Center
Fossil Reviver: Revives any fossil the player may have in their inventory · Inside the house east of the Gurun Town KBT Expressway entrance
Hard Stone to Gem Trader: Gives the player any type of Gem in exchange for Hard Stones · 20 Hard Stones · Inside of the house directly behind the Gurun Town Pokémon Center
Magnolia Egg Lady: Gives away and sells eggs · 50,000-100,000 Poke Dollars · Sits outside the Magnolia Town Cafe depending on the time and day

Nature Changers: Changes the nature of the select Pokemon · Tehl Town NPC : 50,000 Poke Dollars Battle Frontier NPC : 50 Battle Points · Inside of the house southwest of the Tehl Town Pokemon Center Behind the stall in the top-left corner of the Battle Frontier
Egg Buyer: Buys eggs from you · +2,000 Pokedollars per egg (paid to you) · Inside of the house west of the Redwood Village Gym
Egg Hatcher: Significantly speeds up the hatching speed of all eggs in the player's party · 12,500 Poke Dollars (increases with repeated use) · Inside of the house west of the Redwood Village Gym

Macho Brace Upgrader: Gives you a Macho Brace and upgrades it in exchange for Everstones · Depends on the Macho Brace's level · Standing next to a tree near the southern-most waterfall on Route 10, just south of the Cave of Being. Requires Surf
Unova Starters Lady: Gives players the Unova starters for free · Inside the west-most house of Route 5, just west of the Day Care Center

Egg Move Transfer Tutor: Transfers egg moves between two Pokemon of the same evolutionary line · 25,000 Poke Dollars · Inside the side room of the Day Care Center. Only appears after reaching Dehara City
Plate Maker: Gives you all types of creation plates in exchange for shards · Inside Captain Davy's Shipyard at the Seaport City Harbor
Alola Starters Lady: Gives you the Alolan starters for free · Inside the house west of the Seaport City KBT Expressway entrance
IV Changer: Maxes one or all IVs of a selected Pokémon · 1 Stat's IV = 1 Bottle Cap All Stats IVs = 1 Gold Bottle Cap · Near the Seaport City Port by the water

Amulet Coin/Luck Incense Upgrader: Upgrades the player's Amulet Coin and Luck Incense in exchange for Big Nuggets · Depends on the Amulet Coin's level · Standing in the center of Tehl Town near the statue
Name Rater: Allows you to change a Pokémon's nickname · free · Inside the south-most house in town
Power Items Upgrader: Upgrades your Power Items in exchange for Star Pieces and Comet Shards · Depends on the level of the Power Items · East of Antisis City but outside Thundercap Mountain

Normalium Z: Once per battle for the team, turns a Normal attack into Breakneck Blitz (power depends on the move), or adds a Normal status move's Z bonus. Deals 1/4 damage through Protect. Not used up.
Notebook: A notebook containing research on Pokémon moves. Inside it’s marked “Property of Prof. Log’s Aide”.
Nugget: A nugget of pure gold. Can be sold at a high price.
Occa Berry: A hold item that weakens a Fire move if weak to it.
Halves the damage of one super-effective Fire hit. Eaten before that hit; protects against only one hit of a multi-hit move.
Odd Incense: A hold item that boosts Psychic-type moves.
Old Rod: Use by any body of water to fish for wild Pokémon.
Oran Berry: A hold item that restores 10 HP in battle.
At 1/2 max HP or less, restores 10 HP. Eaten once.
Orange Mail: A Zigzagoon-print Mail to be held by a Pokémon.
Oval Charm: Raises the chance of finding eggs at the daycare.
Oval Stone: Peculiar stone that evolves a certain Pokémon.
PP Max: Raises the PP of a move to its maximum points.
PP Up: Raises the maximum PP of a selected move.
Pamtre Berry: {POKEBLOCK} ingredient. Plant in loamy soil to grow Pamtre.
Passho Berry: A hold item that weakens a Water move if weak to it.
Halves the damage of one super-effective Water hit. Eaten before that hit; protects against only one hit of a multi-hit move.
Payapa Berry: A hold item that weakens a Psychic move if weak to it.
Halves the damage of one super-effective Psychic hit. Eaten before that hit; protects against only one hit of a multi-hit move.
Pearl: A pretty pearl that would sell at a cheap price.
Peat Block: A block of material that makes some Pokémon evolve.
Pecha Berry: A hold item that heals poisoning in battle.
Cures poison, including bad poison. Eaten once.
Persim Berry: A hold item that heals confusion in battle.
Pidgeotite: This stone enables Pidgeot to Mega Evolve in battle.
Pikanium Z: Upgrade Pikachu's Volt Tackle into a Z-Move.
Once per battle for the team, Pikachu's Volt Tackle becomes Catastropika: 210-power Electric damage. Not used up.
Pikashunium Z: Upgrade Pikachu w/ a cap's Thunderbolt into a Z-Move.
Once per battle for the team, cap-wearing Pikachu's Thunderbolt becomes 10,000,000 Volt Thunderbolt: 195-power Electric damage with +2 critical-hit stages. Not used up.
Pinap Berry: {POKEBLOCK} ingredient. Plant in loamy soil to grow Pinap.
Pinsirite: This stone enables Pinsir to Mega Evolve in battle.
Poison Barb: A hold item that raises the power of Poison-type moves.
Poison Gem: Increases the power of Poison Type moves.
The first damaging Poison move does 1.3× damage; the gem is used up.
Poisonium Z: Once per battle for the team, turns a Poison attack into Acid Downpour (power depends on the move), or adds a Poison status move's Z bonus. Deals 1/4 damage through Protect. Not used up.
Poké Ball: A tool used for catching wild Pokémon.
Catch rate ×1: the standard catch rate.
Pomeg Berry: Makes a Pokémon friendly but lowers base HP.
Porta-PC: A device that allows you to access the Pokémon storage system. There are some places where it won’t work.
Potion: Restores the HP of a Pokémon by 20 points.
Power Anklet: A hold item that promotes Spd gain, but reduces Speed.
Power Band: Hold item that promotes Sp. Def gain, but reduces Speed.
Power Belt: A hold item that promotes Def gain, but reduces Speed.
Power Bracer: A hold item that promotes Atk gain, but reduces Speed.
Power Herb: Allows immediate use of a move that charges first.
Skips the charging turn of a two-turn move, including Geomancy. Used up; does not skip Solar Beam's bad-weather damage penalty.
Power Lens: Hold item that promotes Sp. Atk gain, but reduces Speed.
Power Weight: A hold item that promotes HP gain, but reduces Speed.
Pretty Wing: Though this feather is beautiful, it's just a regular feather and has no effect on Pokémon.
Primarium Z: Upgrade Primarina's Sparkling Aria into a Z-Move.
Once per battle for the team, Primarina's Sparkling Aria becomes Oceanic Operetta: 195-power Water damage. Not used up.
Prism Scale: A mysterious scale that evolves a certain Pokémon.
Prison Bottle: A bottle used to seal a certain Pokémon long ago.
Protective Pads: Guard the holder from contact move effects.
Prevents contact-triggered effects against the holder, such as Rocky Helmet damage, Static and King's Shield's Attack drop.
Protector: Loved by a certain Pokémon. It's stiff and heavy.
Protein: Raises the base Attack stat of one Pokémon.
Psychic Gem: Increases the power of Psychic Type moves.
The first damaging Psychic move does 1.3× damage; the gem is used up.
Psychic Seed: Boosts Sp. Def. on Psychic Terrain, but only one time.
In Psychic Terrain, raises Sp. Def by 1 stage, even if airborne. Used up; the boost remains after the terrain ends.
Psychium Z: Once per battle for the team, turns a Psychic attack into Shattered Psyche (power depends on the move), or adds a Psychic status move's Z bonus. Deals 1/4 damage through Protect. Not used up.
Pure Incense: A hold item that helps repel wild Pokémon.
Qualot Berry: Makes a Pokémon friendly but lowers base Defense.
Quick Ball: Works well if used on the first turn.
Catch rate ×5 on the first turn of a wild battle, ×1 afterward.
Quick Claw: A hold item that occasionally allows the first strike.
Each turn, has a 20% chance to move first within its priority bracket, regardless of Speed or Trick Room. Does not outrun a higher-priority move.
Quick Powder: A hold item that raises the Speed of Ditto.
Doubles Ditto's Speed, but stops working after Transform.
Rabuta Berry: {POKEBLOCK} ingredient. Plant in loamy soil to grow Rabuta.
Rare Candy: Raises the level of a Pokémon by one.
Rawst Berry: A hold item that heals a burn in battle.
Razor Claw: A hooked claw that ups the holder's critical-hit ratio.
Raises the holder's critical-hit rate by 1 stage.
Razor Fang: A hold item that may cause flinching when the foe is hit.
Damaging moves without a built-in flinch chance gain a 10% flinch chance per hit. Only stops a target that has not acted.
Razz Berry: {POKEBLOCK} ingredient. Plant in loamy soil to grow Razz.
Reaper Cloth: Loved by a certain Pokémon. Imbued with spirit energy.
Red Card: Switches out the foe if they hit the holder.
After surviving a damaging move, forces the attacker into a random teammate. Used up; waits until all hits finish and can stop U-turn or Volt Switch choosing its switch.
Red Nectar: Flower nectar that changes the form of certain Pokémon.
Red Orb: A red, glowing orb said to contain an ancient power.
Red Shard: A shard from an ancient item. Can be sold cheaply.
Repeat Ball: A Ball that works better on Pokémon caught before.
Catch rate ×3.5 if the target's species is already marked caught in your Pokédex, ×1 otherwise.
Repel: Repels weak wild Pokémon for 100 steps.
Retro Mail: Mail featuring the drawings of three Pokémon.
Reveal Glass: This glass returns a Pokémon back to its original form.
Revive: Revives a fainted Pokémon with half its HP.
Rindo Berry: A hold item that weakens a Grass move if weak to it.
Halves the damage of one super-effective Grass hit. Eaten before that hit; protects against only one hit of a multi-hit move.
Ring Target: Moves that usually have no effect will hit the holder.
Removes the holder's type-based immunities, letting Normal hit Ghost or Ground hit Flying. Does not remove ability immunities such as Levitate.
Rock Incense: A hold item that raises the power of Rock-type moves.
Rockium Z: Once per battle for the team, turns a Rock attack into Continental Crush (power depends on the move), or adds a Rock status move's Z bonus. Deals 1/4 damage through Protect. Not used up.
Rocky Helmet: Hurts the foe if they touch its holder.
Each contact hit costs the attacker 1/6 of its own max HP. Triggers on every hit of a multi-hit move; Magic Guard prevents the damage.
Room Service: Lowers Speed if Trick Room is active.
When Trick Room is active, lowers the holder's Speed by 1 stage. Used up.
Rose Incense: A hold item that raises the power of Grass-type moves.
Roseli Berry: A hold item that weakens a Fairy move if weak to it.
Halves the damage of one super-effective Fairy hit. Eaten before that hit; protects against only one hit of a multi-hit move.
S.S. Ticket: The ticket required for sailing on a ferry.
Sablenite: This stone enables Sableye to Mega Evolve in battle.
Sachet: A sachet of strong perfumes, loved by a certain Pokémon.
Sacred Ash: Fully revives and restores all fainted Pokémon.
Safety Goggles: Protect from weather damage and powder moves.
Blocks powder moves, Effect Spore and weather damage from sandstorm and hail.
Salac Berry: A hold item that raises Speed in a pinch.
At 1/4 max HP or less, raises Speed by 1 stage. Gluttony triggers it at 1/2 HP instead. Eaten once.
Salamencite: This stone enables Salamence to Mega Evolve in battle.
Sceptilite: This stone enables Sceptile to Mega Evolve in battle.
Scizorite: This stone enables Scizor to Mega Evolve in battle.
Scope Lens: A hold item that improves the critical-hit rate.
Raises the holder's critical-hit rate by 1 stage.
Sea Incense: A hold item that slightly boosts Water-type moves.
Shadow Mail: A Duskull-print Mail to be held by a Pokémon.
Sharp Beak: A hold item that raises the power of Flying-type moves.
Sharpedonite: This stone enables Sharpedo to Mega Evolve in battle.
Shed Shell: Allows the holder to switch out without fail.
Lets the holder switch out despite trapping moves or abilities. Does not let it flee from wild battles.
Shiny Charm: A charm that will raise the chance of Shiny Pokémon.
Shiny Stone: Makes certain species of Pokémon evolve.
Shuca Berry: A hold item that weakens a Ground move if weak to it.
Halves the damage of one super-effective Ground hit. Eaten before that hit; protects against only one hit of a multi-hit move.
Silk Scarf: A hold item that raises the power of Normal-type moves.
Silvally Memory: A memory disc that changes the type of Silvally and its Multi-Attack.
Silver Powder: A hold item that raises the power of Bug-type moves.
Sitrus Berry: A hold item that restores the user's HP a little.
Eaten when the holder drops to 1/2 HP or less: restores 1/4 of its max HP. Once.
Slowbronite: This stone enables Slowbro to Mega Evolve in battle.
Smoke Ball: A hold item that assures fleeing from wild Pokémon.
Lets the holder flee from wild battles, even through trapping. Does not let it switch out of trapping.
Smooth Rock: Extends the length of Sandstorm if used by the holder.
Sandstorm started by the holder lasts 8 turns instead of 5. Switching out does not shorten it.
Snorlium Z: Upgrade Snorlax's Giga Impact into a Z-Move.
Once per battle for the team, Snorlax's Giga Impact becomes Pulverizing Pancake: 210-power Normal damage. Not used up.
Snowball: Raises Atk if its holder is hit by an Ice-type move.
After surviving an Ice hit, raises Attack by 1 stage. Used up.
Soft Sand: A hold item that raises the power of Ground-type moves.
Solganium Z: Upgrade Solgaleo's Sunsteel Strike into a Z-Move.
Once per battle for the team, Solgaleo or Dusk Mane Necrozma's Sunsteel Strike becomes Searing Sunraze Smash: 200-power Steel damage that ignores abilities. Not used up.
Soothe Bell: A hold item that calms spirits and fosters friendship.
Spell Tag: A hold item that raises the power of Ghost-type moves.
Spelon Berry: {POKEBLOCK} ingredient. Plant in loamy soil to grow Spelon.
Star Piece: A red gem shard. It would sell for a very high price.
Stardust: Beautiful red sand. Can be sold at a high price.
Starf Berry: A hold item that sharply boosts a stat in a pinch.
At 1/4 max HP or less, raises a random stat by 2 stages, excluding accuracy and evasion. Gluttony triggers it at 1/2 HP instead. Eaten once.
Stat Scanner: This special device can analyze the EVs and IVs of a Pokémon in your party.
Steel Memory: A disc with Steel type data. It swaps Silvally's type.
With RKS System, makes Silvally and Multi-Attack Steel type. Does not boost damage.
Steelium Z: Once per battle for the team, turns a Steel attack into Corkscrew Crash (power depends on the move), or adds a Steel status move's Z bonus. Deals 1/4 damage through Protect. Not used up.
Steelixite: This stone enables Steelix to Mega Evolve in battle.
Sticky Barb: Damages the holder each turn. May latch on to foes.
At each turn's end, the holder loses 1/8 max HP. Transfers to an attacker with no held item when it lands a contact move.
Sun Stone: Makes certain species of Pokémon evolve.
Super Potion: Restores the HP of a Pokémon by 60 points.
Super Repel: Repels weak wild Pokémon for 200 steps.
Super Rod: The best fishing rod for catching wild Pokémon.
Swampertite: This stone enables Swampert to Mega Evolve in battle.
Sweet Apple: A very sweet apple that makes certain Pokémon evolve.
Swift Wing: An item for use on a Pokémon. It slightly increases the base Speed stat of a single Pokémon.
Tamato Berry: Makes a Pokémon friendly but lowers base Speed.
Tanga Berry: A hold item that weakens a Bug move if weak to it.
Halves the damage of one super-effective Bug hit. Eaten before that hit; protects against only one hit of a multi-hit move.
Tapunium Z: Upgrade the tapus' Nature's Madness into a Z-Move.
Once per battle for the team, a Tapu's Nature's Madness becomes Guardian of Alola: removes 3/4 of the target's current HP. Not used up.
Tart Apple: A very tart apple that makes certain Pokémon evolve.
Terrain Extender: Extends the length of the active battle terrain.
Terrain started by the holder lasts 8 turns instead of 5. Switching out does not shorten it.
Thick Club: A hold item that raises Cubone or Marowak's Attack.
Doubles Cubone's and Marowak's Attack, including Alolan Marowak.
Throat Spray: Raises Sp. Atk. if the holder uses a sound-based move.
After the holder successfully uses a sound move, raises Sp. Atk by 1 stage. Used up; works with sound-based status moves too.
Thunder Stone: Makes certain species of Pokémon evolve.
Time Turner: A strange device that lets you distort the fabric of time. AM times become PM times and vice versa.
Timer Ball: A Ball that gains power in battles taking many turns.
Catch rate starts at ×1 and gains about ×0.3 per completed turn, up to ×4 after 10 turns.
Tiny Mushroom: A plain mushroom that would sell at a cheap price.
Toxic Orb: A bizarre orb that badly poisons the holder in battle.
Badly poisons the holder at each turn's end if it has no status and can be poisoned. Poison Heal restores 1/8 max HP each turn instead of poison damage. Not used up.
Trainer Catalogue: A device used to find trainers eager for battle in Borrius. It also keeps a record of their teams.
Tropic Mail: A Bellossom-print Mail to be held by a Pokémon.
Twisted Spoon: A hold item that boosts Psychic-type moves.
Tyranitarite: This stone enables Tyranitar to Mega Evolve in battle.
Ultra Ball: A better Ball with a higher catch rate than a Great Ball.
Ultranecrozium Z: This is a crystallized form of Z-Power. It upgrades Necrozma's Photon Geyser to a Z-Move.

Lets Dusk Mane or Dawn Wings Necrozma Ultra Burst. Once per battle for the team, Ultra Necrozma turns Photon Geyser into Light That Burns the Sky: 200 power, using its higher attacking stat; ignores abilities. Not used up.
Up-Grade: A peculiar box made by Silph Co.
Utility Umbrella: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This sturdy umbrella protects the holder from the effects of weather.
Rain and sun do not modify damage or accuracy of incoming moves. The holder's own attacks still use the weather; blocks weather healing or damage from abilities such as Dry Skin.
VS Seeker: A rechargeable unit that flags battle-ready Trainers.
Venusaurite: This stone enables Venusaur to Mega Evolve in battle.
Wacan Berry: A hold item that weakens a Electric move if weak to it.
Halves the damage of one super-effective Electric hit. Eaten before that hit; protects against only one hit of a multi-hit move.
Water Gem: Increases the power of Water Type moves.
The first damaging Water move does 1.3× damage; the gem is used up.
Water Stone: Makes certain species of Pokémon evolve.
Waterium Z: Once per battle for the team, turns a Water attack into Hydro Vortex (power depends on the move), or adds a Water status move's Z bonus. Deals 1/4 damage through Protect. Not used up.
Watmel Berry: {POKEBLOCK} ingredient. Plant in loamy soil to grow Watmel.
Wave Incense: A hold item that slightly boosts Water-type moves.
Wave Mail: A Wailmer-print Mail to be held by a Pokémon.
Weakness Policy: If hit by a super-effective move, ups Atk and Sp. Atk.
After surviving a super-effective hit, raises Attack and Sp. Atk by 2 stages each. Used up; can activate between hits of a multi-hit move.
Wepear Berry: {POKEBLOCK} ingredient. Plant in loamy soil to grow Wepear.
Whipped Dream: A soft and sweet treat loved by a certain Pokémon.
White Herb: A hold item that restores any lowered stat.
Restores all negative stat stages to 0, then is used up. Keeps positive stages; clears both Defense drops from Shell Smash at once.
Wide Lens: A magnifying lens that boosts the accuracy of moves.
Wiki Berry: A hold item that restores HP but may confuse.
At 1/4 max HP or less, restores 1/3 max HP. Confuses a holder whose nature lowers Sp. Atk; Gluttony triggers it at 1/2 HP instead. Eaten once.
Wise Glasses: A pair of glasses that ups the power of special moves.
Wishing Piece: Throw into a {PKMN} Den to attract Dynamax Pokémon.
Wood Mail: A Slakoth-print Mail to be held by a Pokémon.
X Accuracy: Sharply raises move accuracy during one battle.
Raises the active Pokémon's accuracy by 2 stages. Used up; the boost ends on switching out.
X Attack: Sharply raises stat Attack during one battle.
Raises the active Pokémon's Attack by 2 stages. Used up; the boost ends on switching out.
X Defense: Sharply raises stat Defense during one battle.
Raises the active Pokémon's Defense by 2 stages. Used up; the boost ends on switching out.
X Sp. Atk: Sharply raises stat Sp. Atk during one battle.
Raises the active Pokémon's Sp. Atk by 2 stages. Used up; the boost ends on switching out.
X Sp. Def: Sharply raises stat Sp. Def during one battle.
Raises the active Pokémon's Sp. Def by 2 stages. Used up; the boost ends on switching out.
X Speed: Sharply raises stat Speed during one battle.
Raises the active Pokémon's Speed by 2 stages. Used up; the boost ends on switching out.
Yache Berry: A hold item that weakens a Ice move if weak to it.
Halves the damage of one super-effective Ice hit. Eaten before that hit; protects against only one hit of a multi-hit move.
Yellow Shard: A shard from an ancient item. Can be sold cheaply.
Zinc: Raises the base Sp. Def stat of one Pokémon.
Zoom Lens: If the holder moves after the foe, it'll boost accuracy.
The holder's moves have 1.2× accuracy when the target has already acted this turn.
Zygarde Cell: A cell of the Zygarde Pokémon.

There's a constant FOG weather effect during the battle that reduces accuracy of all Pokemon on the battlefield by 40% (20% in Battle Frontier). You can get rid of the weather by setting up a different one (like Hail or Sandstorm) but the fog WILL come back once another weather stops. Pokemon with abilities Infiltrator, Keen Eye or holding an Utility Umbrella are immune to the accuracy loss. You can also get rid of the fog effect completely by using the move Defog.
